ROOTE ORIGIN SYSTEM
01
Roote OriginSystem
Minimum viable product (MVP)and three design directions
Ube Farm CooperativeDavao, Philippines
Client discussion3 October 2026
Illustrative concept photo

Farm discovery and batch origin
Help people discover partner farms and follow the recorded origin of each produce batch.
ROOTE ORIGIN SYSTEM
02
Farm and produce catalogue
Discover approved farms, crops and batch availability. Find a farm or published batch by ID, QR or partner link.
Protected member portal
Growers, processors and recipients manage their assigned records. Administrators control access and publication.
Connected batch history
Record farming details, harvest dates and quantities, then link each batch to its processor and intended brand owner or distributor.
Consumer QR summaries
Publish a selected summary for each batch. Consumers scan it at a cafe, restaurant or on packaging without logging in.
Starting with ube. Members record quantities and availability through the dashboard.

A sample batch journey

ROOTE ORIGIN SYSTEM
06
From Root to Story
A forest-green world where one vine connects origin lookup, partner farms and the cooperative.
Discovery
A prominent leaf holds farm or batch lookup. Farm previews follow the vine down to the people behind the roots.
Proposed scroll behavior
A root drops beside the green trellis. The vine rises to the lookup leaf, then the scroll descends through stories, partner farms and leadership.
Static design concept. Illustrative imagery and sample records. Motion and mobile layouts are proposed.

The vine journey and origin lookup
The new opening makes lookup visible within the connected plant story.
ROOTE ORIGIN SYSTEM
07
Lookup in the leaf
Enter a farm or batch ID, or scan its QR, to open the corresponding public page.
Farms along the vine
Scroll downward through the cooperative story and partner farm previews.
People at the roots
The soil and root section introduces cooperative leadership.
Static design concept. Illustrative imagery and sample records. Motion and mobile layouts are proposed.

ROOTE ORIGIN SYSTEM
08
Grown Together in Davao
Warm grower photography and an early farm directory make the cooperative easy to explore.
Discovery
Visitors search farms or produce, filter the catalogue and open a farm profile. A separate lookup area resolves farm and batch IDs.
Proposed scroll behavior
Photographs reveal gently as the page moves. Farm records settle into readable rows, while origin lookup stays easy to reach.
Static design concept. Illustrative imagery and sample records. Motion and mobile layouts are proposed.

Growers, farms and a clear next step
The editorial opening leads directly into the catalogue and batch lookup.
ROOTE ORIGIN SYSTEM
09
Meet the growers
A warm portrait and a clear farm link introduce the cooperative.
Browse the catalogue
Search farms or produce, then filter by crop and location.
Open the origin
Farm and batch IDs lead to the right public profile or approved summary.
Static design concept. Illustrative imagery and sample records. Motion and mobile layouts are proposed.

ROOTE ORIGIN SYSTEM
10
Purple to the World
Bold purple-yam imagery leads into the recorded origin behind each harvest.
Discovery
A sample batch summary introduces the farm, harvest, processor and recipient. Visitors can explore produce or find a specific batch.
Proposed scroll behavior
The yam moves as the product story opens into its origin record. Purple and pale sections guide visitors toward farms and batch lookup.
Static design concept. Illustrative imagery and sample records. Motion and mobile layouts are proposed.

The product and its recorded origin
A strong product opening connects visitors to the batch information behind it.
ROOTE ORIGIN SYSTEM
11
Ube in focus
The crop takes center stage with routes to produce and batch discovery.
A clear origin record
An illustrative summary shows a farm, harvest, processor and recipient.
Continue to a farm
Public farm and batch links connect the product to its growing story.
Static design concept. Illustrative imagery and sample records. Motion and mobile layouts are proposed.

Choosing the public experience
All three directions use the proposed catalogue, member portal and batch QR features. Select one for implementation.

Direction
What it emphasizes
What it needs
From Root to Story

Botanical assets, motion and mobile testing

Proposed delivery: Weeks 1 to 5
Target: 10 weeks, subject to the selected design, agreed working availability and confirmed pilot workflow.
ROOTE ORIGIN SYSTEM
13
Week
Milestone
Planned output
Week 1
Confirm the system
Confirm one design, pilot records, roles, public fields and whether processors combine harvests.
Week 2
Build the foundation
Build MongoDB, the Express/Node.js API and sign-in. Test account access and role restrictions.
Week 3
Organize the ecosystem
Build farm, produce, partner and account forms. Test saving, editing and permitted access.
Week 4
Capture farming details
Add planting, plot and care records. Test required fields, dates and record corrections.
Week 5
Track harvest batches
Add harvest IDs, quantities and status. Review the growing-to-harvest workflow with pilot users.
Confirm the chosen redesign before kickoff. Testing starts during development in Week 2.

Proposed delivery: Weeks 6 to 10
Target: 10 weeks, subject to the selected design, agreed working availability and confirmed pilot workflow.
ROOTE ORIGIN SYSTEM
14
Week
Milestone
Planned output
Week 6
Connect processing & recipients
Link processors, lots and recipients. Test origin links and each participant's permitted access.
Week 7
Publish the consumer view
Build public summaries, approvals and QR downloads. Test published, private and unknown IDs.
Week 8
Connect the landing experience
Connect the catalogue and chosen design. Check mobile, QR and reduced motion. First review round.
Week 9
Review & accept the pilot
Complete the second review round, pilot acceptance and final workflow, permission and device checks.
Week 10
Launch & transfer
Launch with HTTPS and backups. Check restore, train operators and confirm the support handover.
Review rounds are proposed for Weeks 8 and 9. Client feedback or scope changes may move launch.

Proposed delivery and support
Confirm these arrangements after selecting how we will work together.

15
Proposed delivery items
HTTPS production deployment
Database backups and one restore check
Source files and operator documentation
One training session and two revision rounds
30 days of support for delivered defects
Pilot scope to confirm
Farm catalogue with manually recorded quantities and availability
One harvest batch per processed lot, pending workflow confirmation
QR artwork included. Partners handle physical printing
E-commerce, full ERP stock control and external integrations need separate scope
Combining harvests or adding new workflows requires revised scope and delivery planning.

Pilot acceptance and client inputs
Proposed acceptance checks for the pilot, to confirm before development starts.
ROOTE ORIGIN SYSTEM
16
Acceptance checks
A complete farming-to-recipient batch journey
Saved records after refresh and re-login
Enforced public and private access
Correct production QR destinations
Mobile, keyboard and reduced-motion checks
Client inputs
Approved identity, photographs and leadership roles
Sample farm, batch and partner records
Confirmed processing workflow and visibility rules
Deployment accounts and one review contact
Proposed assisted setup: 10 farms, 20 batches and 25 accounts. Ordinary records can be added afterward.

How should we work together?

17
Will this be project-based, a service contract for an agreed period, or direct employment?
Project-based
Deliver the defined MVP through agreed milestones and a handover.
Does the engagement end after MVP acceptance and launch support?
Service contract
Provide development and support over an agreed period.
What duration, work commitment and ongoing support do you expect?
Direct employment
Join the team in a role that supports the system and broader priorities.
What role, reporting line and responsibilities do you have in mind?

Decisions for the client discussion

Which of the three directions best represents the cooperative?
Pilot workflow

Working arrangement
Project-based, a service contract for an agreed period, or direct employment?

Confirm the design, workflow and working arrangement before finalizing scope and delivery dates.

MongoDB, Express, React and Node.js 26, with TypeScript across the frontend and backend.
